title: Dark 65
opening: The notebook is on the bench. Let me try to read it.

intro.p: For forty years Dadu made chocolate in the workshop behind the shutters. Since the funeral, they have stayed down.

talk: Laila beta! Open up, it is me, Rafiq.
Rafiq Bhai? The shop has been closed for weeks.
I know, I know. But it is Mishti's birthday on Tuesday, and all she wants is your Dadu's dark bar.
One kilo, beta. You remember how he made it, don't you?
I never learned. But he wrote everything in the notebook.
Oh no. The roof leaked last monsoon. The pages are stained, smudged and torn.
Fine. I will work it out from whatever Dadu left behind.

lines.text: {blank} the beans till the whole room smells like toasted bread. Stop before the smoke.
{blank} them to crack the shells and blow the husk away. [[q:The husk is bitter. Give it to the pigeons.]]
{blank} the nibs with the sugar till it pours like thick paste. Dark [[blur:sixty-five]] means that many of every hundred is cacao.
{blank} [[torn:…it overnight, till the sour goes smooth.]] Start when the shutters come down. Stop at the first azaan.
{blank} Melt to the red tape. Cool to the blue. Bring it back up to the green. [[b:Never skip the cool.]]
Pour into the moulds. Tap the tray to knock the air out.

workshop.sceneAlt: Dadu's chocolate workshop at dusk. Tap the glowing objects to remember.
workshop.hintLine: Tap the glowing spots. Dadu left clues all over the workshop.

clues.title: Dadu's apron
clues.text: It still smells of roasted beans. There is a wrapper in the pocket, from the very first bar he ever made.

artText.alt: Dadu's apron with a wrapper in the pocket
artText.label: first bar

clues.title: The sugar jar
clues.text: Dadu's sugar jar. "Weigh it, don't guess," he would say, tapping the lid.

clues.title: The old radio
clues.text: He hummed along to it while the conche turned. It still works, if you hit it just right.

clues.title: Dadu's thermometer
clues.text: Dadu stopped reading the numbers years ago. He put coloured tape where each one lived. The little tag is his reminder for the milk bars, which are a different recipe.

artText.alt: Dadu's thermometer with a red tape marked {red} at 45 degrees, a blue tape marked {blue} at 27 degrees, a green tape marked {green} at 31 degrees, and a tag reading milk: 29

clues.title: The prayer timetable
clues.text: He pinned the prayer times over the bench and circled the first one in pen. It was his alarm clock.

artText.alt: Prayer timetable with Fajr 5:00 am circled in pen
artText.title: Prayer times, Old Dhaka

clues.title: The shop sign
clues.text: The shutters came down at six every evening, even on Fridays. "Chocolate does not care about holidays," he used to say.

artText.alt: A hanging shop sign: open 9 am to 6 pm, shutters down at six sharp

clues.title: Rafiq Bhai's order
clues.text: Still on the spike. Dark 65, one kilo, for his daughter's birthday on Tuesday.

artText.alt: An order slip for Rafiq Bhai, Dark 65, 1 kg

steps.title: Rebuild the line
steps.prompt: Some machine names washed away. Tap a machine, then tap its blank in the notebook. Or drag it there.
steps.say: The page has holes where the machine names washed away. I need to work out which goes where.

machines.name: Conche
machines.does: slowly stirs and airs the chocolate for hours
machines.says: The conche. A slow, warm stir that smooths the chocolate and drives out the sour.

machines.name: Cocoa press
machines.does: squeezes the butter out of the liquor
machines.says: The cocoa press squeezes the butter out of chocolate liquor. Dadu kept his butter in.

machines.name: Roaster
machines.says: The roaster. Hot air tumbles the beans until their smell changes.

machines.name: Tempering table
machines.says: The tempering table. Heat, cool, heat again, so the chocolate sets glossy.

machines.name: Melanger
machines.says: The melanger. Two granite stones turn nibs into paste.

machines.name: Winnower
machines.does: cracks the shells and blows the husk away
machines.says: The winnower. It cracks each bean and a fan carries the husk off.

params.idleInfo: Tap a machine to hear what it does.
params.pickFirst: Pick a machine first, then tap the blank.

placed: Roaster. The smell of the whole workshop starts here.
Melanger. Two stones and a lot of patience.
Conche. The slow part Dadu loved most.
Tempering table. Heat, cool, heat again.
feedback.complete: That is the whole line. Now I have to actually cook it.

hints: Read what each line asks for. Line 2 talks about a husk. Line 5 talks about heat, cool, heat again.
Roaster, winnower, melanger, conche, tempering table, in that order. The cocoa press is not in this recipe.

steps.title: Line 1: roast
steps.prompt: Dadu kept three tins of sample beans. Tap a tin to smell it, then roast the batch to match the notebook.
steps.say: Line 1. Toasted bread, never smoke. Dadu kept sample tins on the shelf.

options.sense: Grassy and sharp, a little sour. Like green mango skin.
options.no: Too green. It still smells raw and sour. The notebook wants toasted bread.

options.sense: Warm toasted bread, with cocoa underneath. Like the first ruti off the tawa.
Smoky and bitter. Like a paratha left on the fire.
options.no: That is smoke. The notebook says to stop before the smoke.

params.idleSense: Tap a tin to smell it.

feedback.correct: Toasted bread. That is it. The whole workshop smells like him.

hints: The notebook wants toasted bread, and to stop before the smoke. Sniff each tin.

steps.title: Line 2: winnow
steps.prompt: Turn the crank to crack the beans and blow the husk away.
steps.say: Line 2. Crack the beans and send the husk to the pigeons.

beat.text: Mmm, I can smell it from the lane! Mind the husk, beta.

feedback.correct: The husk goes to the pigeons. Only nibs left.

steps.title: Line 3: nibs and sugar
steps.prompt: One batch is 1 kg. Slide to decide how much of it is nibs and how much is sugar.
steps.say: Line 3. Nibs and sugar go in the melanger. The order slip should say how much.

feedback.correct: Sixty-five parts cacao, thirty-five parts sugar. It smells rich and sweet.

high.text: Hmm, bitter and chalky, beta. That is more than sixty-five in a hundred.

low.text: Mishti would love it, beta, but it is far too sweet. That is less than sixty-five in a hundred.

hints: Check the order slip in the Workshop tab. How big is the batch, and what does Dark 65 mean?
A 1 kg batch of Dark 65 is 650 g nibs and 350 g sugar.

steps.title: Line 4: conche
steps.prompt: The conche runs overnight. Set how many hours it should turn.
steps.say: Line 4. This part is torn. It says when to start and when to stop.

beat.text: Overnight? Your Dadu never let anyone peek at the conche.

feedback.correct: Eleven hours. Shutters down at six, stopped by the first azaan. The sour has gone smooth.
feedback.near: Close, but Dadu was exact. Check when the shutters come down and when the azaan comes.
feedback.low: In the morning it is still rough and sour on the tongue. It needs longer than that.
feedback.high: By morning the chocolate has gone flat and dull. That is too long.

hints: The notebook says when to start and when to stop. Look for both in the Workshop tab, at the door and on the wall.
The shutters come down at 6 pm. The first azaan, Fajr, is at 5 am. That is 11 hours.

steps.title: Line 5: temper
steps.prompt: Set the three temperatures the notebook asks for, then run the curve. Right ones lock in.
steps.say: Line 5. Three tape colours. Dadu's thermometer must hold the numbers.

beat.text: Is it chocolate yet? Is it, is it?

rows.label: Melt
rows.low: Too cool to melt every crystal. The bar would come out streaky.
rows.high: Too hot. The chocolate would scorch.

rows.label: Cool
rows.low: Too cold. It thickens before it can set properly.
rows.high: Still too warm. The good crystals cannot form yet.

rows.label: Rewarm
rows.low: Too cool. It will set thick and dull.
rows.high: Too warm. It undoes the crystals you just made.

feedback.correct: Forty-five, twenty-seven, thirty-one. The chocolate is glossy and smooth.

hints: The notebook names three tape colours. Look at Dadu's thermometer in the Workshop tab.
Red is 45, blue is 27, green is 31. Ignore the milk tag, this is a dark bar.

steps.title: Last line: mould
steps.prompt: The chocolate is poured. Tap the tray six times to knock the air out.
steps.say: The last line. Pour, then knock the air out.

beat.text: Can I lick the spoon? Please?

feedback.correct: The air is out. Now it just has to set.

talk: "Tastes exactly like it did when I was a boy."
I think I can do this.
recipe: Mould and tap out the air
reveal.realFact: In real life, conching runs from a few hours to over 72 hours.
reveal.next: Chapter 2: Eid. The notebook has a milk chocolate page. It is much more badly stained.
